body.statement: When \(n=2\), \(k=2\), and \(m=1\), Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:matching\text{-}full\text{-}modulus}\) gives \(\Omega_{2,1}(\varepsilon)\asymp\varepsilon^{3/4}\); when \(\varepsilon=0\), it reduces to componentwise circular recovery up to a node permutation, consistent with the exact-identification conclusions of Liang et al. and Varıcı et al. Plateaus are outside Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:finite\text{-}type\text{-}profile}\) and retain their known rotation ambiguity.
body.justification: The reduction records both the flagship \(3/4\) case and the required exact-law sanity check.
body.gap: The exact papers have no rate, while plateau counterexamples do not decide stability at isolated Morse points.
body.consumer: Two-angle systems, including wrapped robotic joint coordinates, receive an interpretable recovery exponent and a clear failure boundary.

obligation.what_is_open: The upper half of the asserted full-class relation \(\Omega_{2,1}(\varepsilon)\asymp\varepsilon^{3/4}\).
obligation.obstruction: Specializing an open full-class rigidity theorem does not prove it, and the radial theorem cannot be substituted for the full primary class.
obligation.attempted: The complete two-node expansion and nonlinear quotient lower bound were audited, and the radial upper bound was proved.
obligation.partial_result: The claimed full-class equality \(\Omega_{2,1}(\varepsilon)\asymp\varepsilon^{3/4}\) inherits the unresolved upper half of Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:matching\text{-}full\text{-}modulus}\). What is proved is \(\Omega_{2,1}(\varepsilon)\ge c\varepsilon^{3/4}\) for every class containing the audited family, together with \(\Omega_{2,1}^{\mathrm{rad}}(\varepsilon)\asymp\varepsilon^{3/4}\). The finite-type condition excludes plateaus, and Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:identification\text{-}hypothesis\text{-}comparison}\) directly proves the zero-law torus conclusion; the cited Euclidean theorems have the same componentwise conclusion type.
